title: Unified Inference: Product PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes (v25)
author: Sofia Ramirez
summary: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements and acceptance criteria), design highlights, roadmap themes, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for Unified Inference v25. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and customer success stakeholders preparing for the v25 release and associated commercial updates.
product_overview:
Overview:

Unified Inference is Redwood Inference's flagship product family that provides a single developer-facing runtime across hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. v25 focuses on three strategic goals: (1) reducing per-token cost for mid-to-large customers via smarter routing and quantization defaults, (2) improving tail-latency predictability for bursty workloads, and (3) simplifying enterprise procurement through new packaging and committed-capacity contracts.

Key capabilities (v25 highlights):
- Cost-aware model routing with per-tenant policy controls (latency vs cost).
- Automatic quantization recommendation profiles per workload class.
- New Dedicated burst model to support short-term capacity spikes.
- Streamlined API for function/tool calling and structured outputs (backwards compatible).

Target users: platform engineering teams, AI-native startups, and enterprise product teams who require predictable unit economics and operational controls for LLM inference.
prd_and_requirements:
Primary goals and measurable outcomes:

1) Reduce average per-token serving cost for P95 customer workloads by 18% when using recommended cost-aware routing and quantization profiles.
2) Maintain P99 token-latency within SLA targets for "low-latency" tier customers (target P99 <= 450ms for common moderation/generation requests).
3) Deliver a simplified pricing and packaging offering that increases commit-based revenue by 25% quarter-over-quarter for Dedicated contracts.

Functional requirements (MUST):
1. Cost-aware routing UI and API: expose routing policy controls (latency_weight, cost_weight, region_preference) via Console and REST. Acceptance: API returns routing_score and applied_variant in response metadata.
2. Quantization profile engine: per-model profiles that can be recommended and auto-applied per tenant. Acceptance: model throughput and accuracy regression tested using standard evals (regression <= 1.0% BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent for generation benchmarks).
3. Dedicated burst capacity: configurable burst window and max-GPU allowance per pool. Acceptance: stress tests show sustained throughput increase and controlled preemption behavior.
4. Pricing & packaging: new 'Committed Dedicated' SKU with tiered discounts and committed-monthly-GPU-hours. Acceptance: billing system produces correct invoices and discount application in sandbox and staging.

Non-functional requirements (SHOULD):
- Telemetry: add token-level cost breakdown and routing reason to Console and logs.
- Backwards compatibility: existing client SDKs continue to work with optional new fields.
- Security: all new config surfaces must be RBAC-protected (roles: tenant-admin, billing-admin).

Metrics and SLOs to measure success:
- Avg per-token cost (USD/token) for cohort customers.
- P99 latency for low-latency tier.
- Committed contract conversion rate.
- Model quality regression rate per eval suite.

Acceptance criteria summary:
- Feature flag gated launch in staging.
- Cross-team signoff from Eng (runtime, infra), Product, Finance, Security, and Customer Success.
- Release checklist completed and runbook available for oncall and account managers.
design_spec:
Design summary and key decisions:

Architecture changes (high level):
- Routing service (new microservice 'router-v2') computes per-request routing_score using inputs: tenant_policy, model_profile, current_load, historical latency, and estimated cost. Router returns selected model_variant and fallback_plan.
- Quantization profile store: profiles stored in config service with schema (model_family, sequence_length_distribution, recommended_quant, expected_latency_delta, quality_regression_pct).
- Dedicated burst implementation: leverage capacity-controller to temporarily upweight burst-capacity pools; integrate with GPU-fleet quotas and preemption policies.

API contract examples (REST response snippet):
- response.metadata.routing: "{\"selected_variant\": \"redwood-gptx-8q\", \"routing_score\": 0.73, \"reason\": \"cost_preference\"}"
- response.metadata.quant_profile: "{\"profile_id\": \"q-prof-3\", \"applied\": true}"

Config table (text):
Parameter | Description | Default | Owner
--- | --- | --- | ---
latency_weight | 0-1 weight favoring lower latency | 0.7 | product/runtime
cost_weight | 0-1 weight favoring lower cost | 0.3 | product/finance
burst_window_seconds | Burst window for Dedicated burst | 600 | infra/scheduling
quant_profile_id | Pointer to quantization profile | null | applied-ml

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Default tenant policies remain unchanged; new controls are opt-in for Hosted customers initially, enabled-by-default for new Dedicated enrollments.
- SDK changes: optional 'routing_policy' parameter added to client constructors; clients without parameter continue using default routing behavior.

Testing and validation:
- Perf bench: run the benchmarking suite (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) with 10 representative workloads. Required result: 18% median cost reduction for prioritized tenant cohort.
- Quality eval: run prompt-sets-and-benchmarks suites and ensure regression <= 1.0% across primary metrics.

Operational considerations:
- Observability: router-v2 emits events for every decision with fields (tenant_id, request_id, selected_variant, lat_est, cost_est, fallback_trigger).
- Traceability: link routing decisions to Console traces and customer-facing billing lines for auditability.

Open design risks:
- Cost estimation variance for novel model families may cause oscillation; mitigation: conservative initial cost estimates and smoothing window.
- Quantization quality regressions for edge-case prompts; mitigation: gated rollout with per-tenant evals and easy rollback.
roadmap_and_themes:
Roadmap themes and milestone timeline (quarterly):

Q2 2028 (Beta):
- Router-v2 beta for select enterprise tenants.
- Quantization profile engine read-only and recommendation mode.
- Console: routing controls UI (tenant policy).

Q3 2028 (GA):
- Dedicated burst GA.
- Committed Dedicated SKU launched with billing integration.
- SDK updates and migration guides published.

Q4 2028 (Optimization & Scale):
- Auto-tune for routing weights based on tenant SLA and cost targets.
- Expand quantization profiles to new model families and add optimizer pipeline for profile suggestions.

Longer-term themes (2029+):
- Cross-region intelligent routing with geopolitical data residency knobs.
- Per-tenant model profiling and automated rollouts based on quality gates.

Milestones and owners:
- Router-v2 implementation complete (Eng: runtime) - target 2028-06-15 - owner: Priya Nair.
- Quantization profile engine MVP - target 2028-06-30 - owner: Daniel Cho.
- Pricing & Billing integration for Committed SKU - target 2028-07-15 - owner: Finance-legal team lead (Eva Stone).

Dependencies and risks:
- Billing API changes must land before GA (dependency: finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process).
- GPU-fleet capacity to support burst windows must be validated (dependency: eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity).
pricing_and_packaging_notes:
Summary of packaging updates (v25):

New SKUs and terms:
1. Hosted API (unchanged): pay-as-you-go per-token pricing with minor discounts for volume. New enhancement: routing-based cost estimates displayed in Console before request.
2. Committed Dedicated (new): monthly committed GPU-hours with tiered discounts. Example tiers: Silver (0-2k GPU-hrs/month, 10% discount), Gold (2k-10k GPU-hrs/month, 20% discount), Platinum (>10k, 30% discount + priority burst).
3. Dedicated Burst (add-on): burst pools billed by peak GPU-hours used during burst windows, capped per-contract.
4. Private (on-prem/VPC): licensing + support fee; optional managed burst and routing features licensed separately.
5. Redwood Optimize (add-on): charged as per-eval or seat-based for on-prem analytics; new 'Auto-quantize' feature priced as a % uplift on token price when enabled for hosted customers.

Pricing examples (illustrative):
- Hosted API: $0.0025 / 1k tokens (standard generation model); routing-based variant may reduce to $0.0020 / 1k tokens for cost-optimized variant.
- Committed Dedicated (Gold): list-price equivalent $0.65 / GPU-hour after 20% discount.

Commercial considerations and billing implementation notes:
- Billing must surface committed discounts and burst usage lines with mapping to tenant policy decisions.
- Sales playbook: update competitive sheet to emphasize predictable unit economics and burst capability.
- Contract language: include explicit burst caps, preemption SLAs, and migration assistance for Private customers.

Packaging guidance for Sales and CS:
- For customers with steady throughput and sensitive SLAs recommend Committed Dedicated Gold or Platinum.
- For startups and low-volume customers recommend Hosted API with routing-cost controls enabled in recommendation mode.

Financial targets:
- Increase committed revenue by 25% QoQ following v25 launch.
- Reduce average hosted per-token cost by 12% across measured cohorts via routing + quantization in first 90 days.
release_notes:
v25 Release Notes (2028-06-01):

Highlights:
- Router-v2: cost-aware routing with per-tenant policy controls (beta->GA for Dedicated).
- Quantization profile engine: default recommendations and opt-in auto-apply.
- Dedicated burst: supports short-term capacity spikes with controlled preemption.
- New Committed Dedicated SKU and billing integration.

Behavioral changes for customers:
- Some requests may be routed to quantized or lower-cost model variants if tenant policy allows; Console shows routing_reason and estimated cost delta.
- Dedicated customers with burst enabled will see new billing lines for burst usage.

Migration and upgrade notes:
- No forced migration required for Hosted customers.
- Dedicated customers upgrading to Committed SKU must sign addendum; migration assistance offered by Solutions Engineering.

Rollback and mitigation plan:
1. Feature-flag controlled rollouts (per-tenant).
2. Immediate rollback: disable router-v2 feature-flag in control plane - route all traffic to router-v1.
3. If billing anomalies detected, disable Committed discount application and open emergency billing ticket.

Monitoring and dashboards to watch post-launch:
- routing_v2.decision_rate and router_v2.error_rate (alert if error_rate > 0.1%).
- quant_profile.quality_regression_rate (alert if > 1.0% across evaluation suite).
- billing.committed-discount-errors count.

Notes for Customer Success and Sales:
- Provide a migration checklist and sample contract language.
- Prepare a one-page summary for customers showing expected cost delta for their historical usage when using recommended settings.

Known issues and workarounds:
- In rare cases sampling-based cost estimates may underpredict peak cost by up to 8% for unusual prompt distributions. Workaround: enable conservative_cost_estimates in tenant policy.
- SDKs older than 2.8.0 will not show routing metadata in responses; recommend upgrading to 2.9.0+.
acceptance_criteria:
The release is considered acceptable when all of the following are met:

- Router-v2 is operational in production for GA customers with error_rate < 0.1% for 72 hours.
- Quantization auto-apply shows quality regression <= 1.0% across the platform eval suite for 14 consecutive days in staging and 7 days in limited production.
- Billing integration passes end-to-end tests including discount application and invoice generation for Committed Dedicated.
- Console surfaces routing decisions and cost estimates with correct RBAC controls.
- Cross-functional signoff documented in release checklist (Product, Eng, Finance, Security, CS).
rollout_steps:
Rollout plan (high-level):

1. Internal canary: enable router-v2 for internal tenants and alpha customers (feature-flag) - duration: 1 week.
2. Limited beta: invite 10 enterprise customers (opt-in) to try router-v2 and quantization auto-apply - duration: 2 weeks.
3. Gradual GA: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% traffic ramp with automated health checks (monitoring thresholds) between steps.
4. Dedicated burst: enable for Dedicated customers who opted into Committed SKU after billing tests passed.
5. Post-launch: 30-day optimization window - collect telemetries and apply tuned profiles and weightings.

Emergency rollback procedure (simplified):
- Toggle off router-v2 via control plane flag.
- Re-route affected tenants to previous model variants and notify CS for impacted accounts.
- Open incident with Eng SRE if billing or quality regressions exceed thresholds.
